h1: The 6 Best Rolling Printer Stands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Rolling Printer Stands 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six rolling printer stands and carts compared on surface size, locking wheels, drawers, footprint and storage for home offices.
summary: The HUANUO is the best rolling printer stand: locking casters, a storage drawer and cable cutouts in a body that slides under a desk. The YAOHUOO gives full-size all-in-ones a 22 by 15 inch deck, and the GYIIYUO combines file drawers with an extended top. Simple Houseware and Pipishell carts are cheap but offer no drawer or cable routing.
intro: A printer on wheels is a different appliance from one bolted to a desk. It frees the work surface, hides in a closet during video calls and rolls to the paper supply when needed. The detail most buyers miss is the locks: casters that spin freely turn every tray pull into a small slide across the floor, and the cart creeps further each time you press a button.

We reviewed eight rolling carts and stands and kept six that can realistically carry a home printer. The order comes from spec sheets: top surface size, whether the casters lock, what storage is included and how much floor each one claims. A stand is only as good as the margin between your printer's footprint and its deck.

products.name: HUANUO Printer Stand with Cable Management and Storage Drawer
products.verdict: A purpose-built printer cart with locking wheels, a drawer and tidy cable routing.
products.description:
The HUANUO is a purpose-built printer cart with locking casters, a built-in drawer, cable management cutouts and a maximum shelf height of 14.1 inches. That height number is the one that decides whether it rolls under a desk, and the locks keep the printer planted while you pull a paper tray.

Locks, a drawer and cable routing arrive in one piece here, and the whole thing costs less than the file cabinets, which earns the top spot. The YAOHUOO offers more deck, but does not highlight wheel locks.

Buy it for a compact home printer that lives under a desk. The caveat is surface area: it has a limited top and does not suit very wide printers, so skip it if you own a full-size office all-in-one. Check your printer's footprint against the deck before ordering.
products.idealFor: Compact home printers that live under a desk.
products.skipIf: Your printer is a full-size office all-in-one.

products.name: YAOHUOO 22"x15" Large Printer Stand with Drawer
products.verdict: Real top-surface room for a full-size all-in-one on wheels.
products.description:
The YAOHUOO is a two-tier rolling table with a 22 by 15 inch top, a built-in drawer and rolling casters, sized for full-size all-in-one printers. A big deck matters because multifunction machines have wide bodies and a pull-out tray that needs clearance on every side, and a top that is too small means feet over the edge.

It ranks second since wheel locks are not highlighted in the listing, which is the one feature the HUANUO leads with. Against the GYIIYUO, it costs less and focuses on the printer, not on filing.

Buy it if you own a large all-in-one and have the floor space. Skip it if space is tight, because the larger footprint takes more room than the HUANUO. Check for locking wheels before you buy.

products.name: GYIIYUO 2 Drawer File Cabinet with 24-Inch Extended Desktop
products.verdict: A rolling file cabinet whose extended top doubles as the printer stand.
products.description:
The GYIIYUO is a rolling file cabinet with two letter and A4 drawers, a 24 inch extended desktop, a side storage bag and fabric drawer fronts. The extension acts as a printer deck and a spare work surface, so one piece replaces both a cabinet and a stand.

It ranks third because it costs more than the carts above, and it is bulkier than an open stand. It does beat the DEVAISE below on width, with a 24 inch top against a fixed cabinet top.

Buy it if you need file storage and a printer base together, such as in a small home office. Skip it if all you want is a platform. The caveat is that the extended portion overhangs the cabinet, so keep the printer over the supported body.
products.idealFor: Home offices that need files and a printer base together.
products.skipIf: You only need a printer platform.

products.name: DEVAISE 3-Drawer Mobile File Cabinet
products.verdict: Three lateral drawers and a flat top, all on casters.
products.description:
The DEVAISE is a three-drawer lateral mobile file cabinet with a rolling caster base, rustic brown finish and a flat top meant for a printer. Lateral drawers hold files side to side and hide everything behind a front, which keeps a printer station looking tidy.

It ranks fourth because it is heavier to move than the carts and its closed drawers hide supplies you reach for often. The GYIIYUO above gives a wider surface for similar money, and the HUANUO is lighter.

Buy it for an office that wants hidden filing under the printer and a warm wood-look finish. Skip it if you prefer open, reachable shelves, since you must open a drawer every time you want paper. Confirm your printer's feet fit the flat top before ordering.
products.idealFor: Offices that want hidden filing under the printer.

products.name: Simple Houseware 3-Tier Heavy Duty Metal Utility Rolling Cart
products.verdict: A flexible steel cart that happens to carry a printer well.
products.description:
The Simple Houseware cart is a three-shelf open metal cart with a heavy duty steel frame, four casters and a white finish. It is a general-purpose utility cart, so the frame is strong and the shelves are reusable for other jobs once you change printers.

It ranks fifth because it has no drawer and no cable management, so cords hang loose and wheels can snag them. The HUANUO and YAOHUOO are built around the printer, while this cart simply tolerates one.

Buy it if you want a flexible steel cart at a very low price. Skip it if cable management and a drawer matter. Tie cords to the frame, leave slack for rolling, and check whether the casters lock before loading a heavy printer.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers wanting a flexible cart.
products.skipIf: You want cable management and a drawer.

products.name: Pipishell 3 Tier Rolling Cart with Wheels and Handle
products.verdict: The narrowest rolling option for a printer in a tight room.
products.description:
The Pipishell is a three-tier open metal cart with four rolling wheels, a built-in push handle and a slim footprint. A narrow body slips into corners and closets, and the handle lets you steer the loaded cart without gripping the printer.

It ranks last because the shelves are narrow and there is no drawer or cable routing. The Simple Houseware has a similar open design with a sturdier steel frame, which is why it edges ahead.

Buy it for a small room with a compact printer. Skip it if your printer is wide, since its feet will overhang the narrow shelves. Measure width and depth against the listing before you commit.
products.idealFor: Small rooms with a compact printer.

whatMatters.detail: The top is the platform your printer sits on, and if its feet hang over the edge it can tip or rock. Measure your printer's width and depth, then add a couple of inches for the paper tray to open. Check the listing for exact surface dimensions rather than overall cart size, such as the YAOHUOO's 22 by 15 inches.

Casters are the small wheels that let the cart roll, and locking ones hold it still. Without locks the cart creeps every time you pull a tray or press a button. Look for the word locking in the specs and note how many of the wheels actually lock, because the HUANUO lists them and several others do not.

A stand that fits under your desk keeps the printer out of the way. Measure your desk's clearance height and compare it with the listed maximum shelf height, such as the HUANUO's 14.1 inches. Remember the printer adds its own height on top, so leave a gap above it for the lid and tray.

Drawers hide clutter but make supplies harder to see, while open shelves keep paper in reach but show everything. Think about whether you reach for paper daily. Check what each tier is listed to hold before buying, and whether the drawer has a stated depth that fits reams or only small items.

A printer needs power and often USB, and loose cords snag on wheels. Cutouts or routing channels keep them tidy and stop the cart from pulling on the outlet when it rolls. Look for cutouts in the title or bullet points. The HUANUO lists them, while open carts leave the cords to you.

cards.text: Cabinets hide files and look tidier, but weigh more and cost more. The GYIIYUO and DEVAISE fit this group, while the HUANUO and YAOHUOO sit between with a single drawer.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to the HUANUO unless they have files to store.

faq.q: Do rolling printer stands work with any printer?
faq.a: Only if the top surface is large enough and the cart is rated for the weight. Measure your printer's footprint first and compare it with the listed top dimensions, such as the YAOHUOO's 22 by 15 inches.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make most often?
faq.a: Skipping the wheel locks. Without them, pulling the paper tray can push the cart away from you, so look for locking casters on the listing. The HUANUO lists them; check the others carefully.

faq.q: Is a file cabinet worth it over a basic cart?
faq.a: If you keep paperwork near the printer, yes. The GYIIYUO gives you two file drawers and a 24 inch top, saving a separate cabinet. If you only need a platform, a cart such as the HUANUO is cheaper and lighter.

faq.q: How do I set up the printer on a cart?
faq.a: Place the printer centered on the top, route the power and USB cords through any cutouts, and lock the casters before you start printing. Give the paper tray room to open on every side.

faq.q: How do I keep cords from tangling?
faq.a: Use the cutouts on the HUANUO, or a cable tie on open carts like the Pipishell, and leave enough slack for the cart to roll a short distance without pulling on the outlet.

faq.q: Can I use a utility cart instead?
faq.a: Yes, the Simple Houseware and Pipishell carts work, but they lack drawers and cable routing, so you manage supplies and cords yourself. They suit buyers who want the lowest price and a cart they can reuse later.

finalTake: The HUANUO is the right rolling printer stand for most homes: it locks, stores supplies and routes cables in a body that tucks under a desk. Choose the YAOHUOO for full-size all-in-ones and the GYIIYUO when files must live nearby. Measure the printer and the deck before ordering, and insist on locking wheels.
